headline: Highest risk is medium: ctx can observe Claude Code events and filesystem while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only, creating limited prompt-injection and data-flow exposure but no direct write or network conflict.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events and has filesystem access, so it can ingest content that may later be treated as instructions. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no active tool surface, so the pathway is one-way and not a shared live channel. The interaction exists in default use, but blast radius is bounded by the docs-only agent.
conditions: IF ctx ingests content from Claude Code events as instructions
IF python-cheatsheet content is copied into ctx-managed context without provenance checks
mitigations: Add provenance tags to imported snippets
Restrict ctx to allowlisted instruction sources
Review event hooks for prompt-like content
Use manual copy review before reuse

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, MCP servers, and filesystem, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no files, APIs, or secrets handled. There is no evidence that python-cheatsheet can exfiltrate data, so leakage is limited to accidental inclusion of ctx-managed content in documentation workflows. The pair does not share a documented workspace or authenticated principal.
conditions: IF ctx-managed logs are manually pasted into python-cheatsheet outputs
IF both agents are run under the same shared workspace with copied files
mitigations: Keep ctx logs out of docs drafts
Separate workspaces for the two agents
Redact runtime logs before reuse
Disable copying sensitive snippets into documentation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can install packages and run browsers, while python-cheatsheet cannot execute shell, write files, or modify git state. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the only overlap is read-only content handling. Because no shared mutable resource or locking primitive is documented, the conflict pathway is weak and mostly operational rather than destructive.
conditions: IF both agents are manually pointed at the same mutable directory
IF ctx is granted write access outside the documented profile
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet read-only
Avoid shared mutable directories
Run ctx in a separate workspace
Document any added write permissions

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx can observe tool events and manage context, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream workflows. python-cheatsheet is a reference/documentation agent, which increases the chance that ctx-produced summaries are reused without verification. The pair lacks a built-in verification step, so errors can cascade into incorrect documentation or actions, though no direct action-taking authority is shown for python-cheatsheet.
conditions: IF ctx summaries are copied into python-cheatsheet content without review
IF downstream automation treats ctx output as source of truth
mitigations: Require human review of ctx outputs
Add citation checks before reuse
Mark generated text as unverified
Keep reference docs separate from agent logs

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only or source-available with no explicit regulated data classes, and python-cheatsheet lists no secrets, OAuth scopes, or residency-sensitive handling. ctx touches audit/runtime logs and MCP servers, so compliance risk is mainly retention or logging policy mismatch if those logs are repurposed into documentation. The other agent is not cited for a specific residency breach because none is documented.
conditions: IF ctx audit/runtime logs contain regulated data and are copied into docs
IF retention rules for ctx logs differ from documentation retention
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from logs
Set a short log-retention window
Review documentation for sensitive excerpts
Add a deletion checklist for reused snippets
